source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check all usb port could detect device
All USB port can be detected  in BIOS/OS

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Make sure the devices can be detected under OS

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: usbutils + operator to attach the device
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Devcie detection: verify device detection in OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsusb 2>&1; ip link 2>&1 | grep -E '^[0-9]+:' | head 2>&1" with the device present; physical setup is operator-owned.  -- USB device-detection sibling row; the OS USB tree check covers the SAME set of ports as the partner row.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the lsusb/device list so the user confirms the devices are detected in OS.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED because device, port and acceptance scope were absent and BIOS-versus-OS scope was unresolved.

original_test_intent: Verify that every project-designated physical USB port can enumerate the approved device set with the expected identity and driver state; the source must clarify whether BIOS detection is also an acceptance requirement or OS detection alone controls.
original_method: An operator connects known-good approved devices to each mapped USB port. The OS USB topology, enumeration, driver binding and error evidence are captured per port; BIOS detection is separately recorded only if the owner confirms that procedure phrase is required scope.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must attach and remove each approved physical device at the mapped ports. OS enumeration and driver evidence can then be automated; if BIOS detection is confirmed as required, an engineer must perform or authorize the platform-specific BIOS interaction and capture its evidence.
required_inputs: Approved non-boot device matrix with VID/PID/serial and expected driver per port type
Operational definition of detected: enumeration, driver binding and any usability requirement
Owner decision whether the BIOS/OS procedure phrase adds BIOS acceptance beyond the OS-only criterion
Operator, maintenance authorization, safe removal and alternate/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not attach arbitrary, bootable, sensitive, service-owned or electrically unsuitable USB devices.
Do not infer all physical ports from one lsusb tree or reuse sibling-case coverage without explicit mapping.
Preserve baseline logs and stop on overcurrent, unexpected mount, input/security change, controller error or access impact.
Safely eject storage after I/O is idle and do not auto-retry an ambiguous or faulty port.
agent_execution_scope: Validate device/port identities and capture USB topology, mounts, driver and kernel/system/BMC baseline.
Coordinate each operator attachment with timestamped per-port enumeration, driver binding, topology and error evidence.
If an approved BIOS capture mechanism exists, organize that evidence separately; compare expected/actual without setting the verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve BIOS-versus-OS scope and approve the port/device/driver matrix.
Perform physical device attachment/removal and any required BIOS UI interaction.
Review per-port coverage and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lsusb is relevant for OS enumeration, but ip link is unrelated to generic USB-device detection, a head-limited snapshot can omit devices, and the sibling-row coverage assertion is unsupported.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use complete, timestamped OS-native USB topology/enumeration and driver-binding evidence correlated to the approved physical port/device matrix; add platform-specific BIOS evidence only after scope confirmation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-port wording, literal BIOS/OS procedure, OS-only criterion and 20/20-minute fields are preserved without silently choosing one conflicting scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a signed per-port/device matrix with complete USB topology, VID/PID/serial, negotiated speed, driver binding and event/error evidence; treat any confirmed BIOS check as a separate manual evidence step.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact platform USB topology and deployed OS; BIOS method is platform specific.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, OS, kernel, USB controller/driver and inventory-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use board USB topology documentation and the deployed OS/vendor device-enumeration documentation supplied for the project.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines identity and per-port proof and surfaces the BIOS/OS discrepancy instead of assuming scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; every approved physical port/device combination remains explicit.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Port/device matrix, detection definition and BIOS-scope decision.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS logical topology does not by itself identify a chassis connector; BIOS visibility may differ by device class and firmware settings.

project_override_considerations: A project may define the device set, port matrix and OS-only or BIOS-plus-OS scope. Completing that plan applies only to the stated matrix; the master source's BIOS/OS wording and OS-only criterion remain unchanged.
expected_evidence: SUT identity, physical port/controller map and approved device/driver/power matrix
Per-port operator timestamp, exact device identity, full topology/enumeration, driver and negotiated-speed evidence
Owner BIOS/OS scope decision and BIOS evidence if required
No unexpected mount/power/controller/service impact, restored state, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure says all USB ports are detected in BIOS/OS, while the criterion requires only OS detection. These are different coverage obligations; owner clarification is required and neither phrase may be silently discarded.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The per-port device-detection intent is clear and the OS portion is executable once project inputs arrive. The BIOS-scope conflict is recorded for owner decision, but missing matrices/specification inputs do not create permanent BLOCKED status under V3.1.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the physical/OS split but removes irrelevant/truncated probes and rejects assumed sibling coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its missing-input and scope concerns but reclassifies BLOCKED to PARTIAL because those are resolvable readiness and owner-scope decisions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records the BIOS/OS discrepancy as a true source conflict while preserving separately executable OS evidence.

review_improvement: Prevents false all-port claims and silent loss of BIOS scope while keeping a clear route to execute the approved project matrix.
independent_technical_reasoning: Physical connection is essential but host enumeration is automatable, so the base classification is PARTIAL. The procedure/criterion discrepancy changes coverage but does not make the entire detection purpose unknowable; it requires a case-specific owner decision rather than permanent BLOCKED.
